model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the perceived most important measures that could be implemented to address the "shadow economy" in a country. The horizontal axis represents the various measures, while the vertical axis indicates the percentage of respondents who believe each measure is important. The bars are color-coded, with blue representing measures that are currently in place and red indicating measures that are not in place. The chart shows that the highest percentage of respondents, 13%, believe that improving the quality of administrative services is the most important measure. This is followed by 10% who think that reducing the activities of mafia organizations is crucial. Other measures, such as strengthening the effectiveness of the tax system, implementing anti-corruption laws, and increasing the effectiveness of business stimuli, also have significant percentages, with 9%, 5%, and 5% respectively. Measures that are currently in place, such as maintaining tax control, providing effective business stimuli, and increasing the number of people paying taxes, have lower percentages, ranging from 2% to 5%. The chart does not provide any information on the actual implementation or effectiveness of these measures, nor does it compare the measures across different countries or regions.
